subject: MAP asks: prefetch/batching simulation and tokens-per-$ sensitivity
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma@acmehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: MAP: we need the tokens/$ breakdown + caching assumptions

Laura — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and our engineering leads want the cost detail pulled into the MAP before we sign the SOW. Two quick asks we need visible in the MAP: 

- Clear tokens-per-dollar assumptions for the recommended model variants (including quantized options).
- How prefix/KV prefetching changes average tokens per user request (you mentioned prefetch gains during the call).
- Expected batch size distribution and how it impacts unit cost at our throughput (estimated 150 reqs/sec peak).

Can you surface a short sensitivity table (high/nominal/low cache hit scenarios) and a proposed close timeline? Procurement would like a draft by next Tuesday if possible.

Also happy to loop engineers on specific simulation outputs.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Liu
Head of Product, Acme Health

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-02T11:04:00Z
Subject: RE: MAP: we need the tokens/$ breakdown + caching assumptions

Emma — appreciate the clarity. Attaching the initial MAP draft and a CSV export of the simulation we ran against your sample traffic profile. High level:

- Baseline model (fp16) nominal: 1.9M tokens = $275 (tokens/$ = ~6,909 tokens per $) — this reflects our steady-state sim with batching and warm KV cache.
- Quantized (int8) fallback: ~20% lower per-token cost but ~+8% latency on tails; we include both in the MAP as Model A / Model A-Quant.
- Prefetch / KV assumptions used: 60% prefix cache hit rate (your sample), prefetch warmup reduces generation tokens by ~18% on average for multi-turn flows.
- Batching: continuous batching model with target batch size 8 at peak; effective batch sizes vary (median 4, p95 9). We show tokens/$ at three batch percentiles in the sensitivity sheet.

Internal: Karthik / Priyom — please review the attached sim CSV and confirm the sensitivity table before I send a final MAP to Emma & procurement. Procurement wants the close timeline in the doc as dates.

Attachments: acme-map-draft-v1.pdf; unit-econ-sim-results.csv

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-03T08:27:00Z
Subject: RE: MAP: we need the tokens/$ breakdown + caching assumptions

Laura / Priyom — quick notes from the sims (attached CSV):

- Assumptions: user-turn distribution from Acme sample yields avg output tokens per request = 180, avg input tokens = 40 => avg total 220 tokens/request nominal.
- Cache effect: with 60% prefix hit, effective generation tokens drop to ~165/request. If we prefetch top-3 likely prefixes (our prefetch heuristic) we see additional ~6-9% token reduction in multi-turn sessions.
- Batching sensitivity: moving median batch from 4 to 8 improves throughput tokens/$ by ~23% in the sim, but increases p99 latency under bursty load — need SLO tradeoff.
- Unit econ: nominal tokens-per/$ at scale (steady-state) = ~6,900 tokens/$ (matches Laura). Low cache case (35% hit) drops to ~5,100 tokens/$; high caching (75% hit) increases to ~8,400 tokens/$.

I added a quick column to unit-econ-sim-results.csv: tokens_per_$_[low|nom|high_cache]. Recommend we ship a sensitivity table with +/-20% cache hit bands and two batching profiles (conservative: median 4, aggressive: median 8).

Also note model fallback: if capacity constrained we route to quantized variant — per-token cost delta is ~-20% but some prompt re-encoding increases tokens by ~2-4% in our sim due to tokenization differences; net savings still ~15-18%.

Karthik
Director, Inference Optimization

From: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-04T14:55:00Z
Subject: RE: MAP: we need the tokens/$ breakdown + caching assumptions

Quick procurement-facing clarifications to include in the MAP before we share externally:

- Please add a short table with the deterministic SLO commitments we can meet per model tier (latency p95, p99) and the impact on tokens/$ when we enforce stricter latency SLOs (e.g., smaller batch sizes). Procurement needs to understand cost vs SLA.
- Create an explicit sensitivity row showing cost impact if cache hit is +/-20% and if prefetch warmup is disabled (edge case).
- Confirm whether any additional licensing or encryption (KMS/HSM) fees would affect unit econ — for Acme we should call out one-time setup costs separately from per-token math.

I'll draft a Procurement blurb and add to the MAP if Karthik / Laura confirm the numbers.

— Priyom
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: MAP: we need the tokens/$ breakdown + caching assumptions — updated MAP and next steps

Emma / Procurement — thanks for the ask and patience. We've consolidated the sim outputs and clarified the MAP:

- Attached: acme-map-draft-v1.pdf (MAP with timelines), unit-econ-sim-results.csv (detailed sims), sensitivity-table-prefetch.xlsx (high/nominal/low cache scenarios + batching profiles).
- Nominal tokens/$: ~6,900 tokens per $ (steady-state, 60% cache hit, median batch 4).
- Sensitivity: cache low (35%) => ~5,100 tokens/$; cache high (75%) => ~8,400 tokens/$. Batching aggressive (median 8) improves tokens/$ by ~23% but increases p99 latency — we included both conservative and aggressive SLO rows.
- Model variants: Model A (fp16) and Model A-Quant (int8 fallback). Quantized variant reduces per-token cost ~20% (net after tokenization delta ~15%).
- Procurement notes: one-time private deployment setup (if chosen) and KMS integration are called out separately in the MAP (no hidden per-token adders).

Proposed MAP timeline (high level):
- 2027-09-09: Final MAP signoff (this doc)
- 2027-09-16: SOW executed / finance + procurement signatures (DocuSign link included)
- 2027-09-23: Pilot kick-off (2-week pilot window)
- 2027-10-07: Pilot readout and decision to scale or iterate

Action items for Acme: quick signoff on the MAP assumptions (cache hit baseline = 60%, batch profile median=4) or provide adjusted traffic profile by 2027-09-09. Once we get that, we'll finalize the SOW and the docusign link.

Attachments are included. Let us know if you want an extra sensitivity run (+/-10% traffic, bursty p95 patterns).

Best regards,
